checks.name: Screen-share quality browser regression
checks.command: cd clients/web && CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH='/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome' npm run test:screen-profile -- --grep 'scenario names stay readable|shows quality choices without hiding them'
assertions: Scenario titles, descriptions, resolution labels and FPS labels fit without clipping at desktop and narrow viewports.
Resolution and FPS choices are visible without opening a disclosure control.

The fixed 60 FPS value appears as a compact badge aligned with its label, without an empty segmented track.
Keyboard ArrowRight from 1080p selects 1440p and switches to the supported text profile.
Header and actions stay in view while the settings body scrolls.
At 390x640, scrolling to the scenario selector places both scenario cards and their full helper labels in the visible dialog viewport.
At 637x584, both scenario cards with labels, the 1440p option and the 30 FPS option are simultaneously within the visible dialog viewport after scrolling to the selector.
The close icon action exposes the accessible name Закрыть; Cancel and Start retain their visible accessible names.

additional_captures.note: Both scenario cards and helper labels are fully visible after scrolling to the selection area.
1440p is selected; the selected profile is 1440p · 30 FPS.
Both scenario cards, all resolution options including selected 1440p, and selected 30 FPS are visible together after scrolling to the selector.

checks.name: Screen-share accessibility and scroll geometry regression

assertions: The settings body scrolls independently while header and footer remain visible.
1440p is enabled and direct selection changes to text mode at 30 FPS.
axe-core reports no scoped WCAG 2.2 AA violations in the setup dialog.
Tab and Shift+Tab move through the dialog controls and wrap to the close/start actions.
